CLOSED. Both call sites this bead named are fixed: signature.scala at 3b246ea, population.scala at
a12fdde. No `Some(view.relativePosition(` remains in any production source.

WHAT THE BEAD GOT WRONG ABOUT ITSELF, kept rather than corrected in the title: it says TWO call
sites. There are THREE. hsmm.scala:56-57 reads relativePosition RAW, which my grep for the
`Some(view.relativePosition(r))` shape could not see. Split out as
bd-01M17Y03XGDD0XR26PN41TJVRJ and claimed by scout, whose candidate 7ee4872 answers the design
question I left open there -- sparse absence that abstains numerically while staying distinct in
the diagnostic map, with Some(0.0) retained so measured zero is not absence.

Delivered beyond the original scope: SourceView.measuredPosition: Option[Double] as the named
accessor (the pattern already existed unnamed in embed-bench/metrics.scala), relativePosition
reduced to a visible getOrElse over it, and the totality docstring corrected -- it still described
the two call sites as laundering after they had stopped.

EVIDENCE: alignJVM 212, lawsJVM 86, GATE_EXIT=0; JVM/JS/Native all green for 3b246ea
(1453 tests); scalafmtCheckAll separate and clean on both commits. The accessor is mutation-proved
at SignatureSuite; neither call site has a dedicated control, because SourceViewLaws makes the
violation unreachable for both real implementations -- stated as a gap rather than papered over.
